subject: Activation fastlane: MAP and GPU pool sizing for HelixHealth
messages:
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procure@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Activation fastlane: MAP and GPU pool sizing for HelixHealth

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I’m pulling together a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that aligns HelixHealth’s evaluation sprint to a committed capacity activation. The goal: get a lightweight CAN (commit-and-notify) path so you can start a private deployment with predictable throughput within the quarter.

Quick asks so we can finalize the MAP template (attached: initial_map_fastlane.xlsx):
- Confirm target go-live window (you mentioned mid-June). Is that still accurate?
- Preferred deployment: Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU pools) or Private (VPC + customer-managed infra)?
- Expected peak concurrent production RPS and average sequence length for LLM workloads (approx tokens per request).
- Any procurement blackout windows or internal signoff dates we should respect?

High-level guidance we’ll map into the plan:
- Lead time assumptions: H100-class capacity ~12–14 weeks from order to activation; for smaller Ampere/RTX nodes estimate 6–8 weeks.
- Staging buffer: recommend a 20–30% buffer in the initial GPU pool to absorb evaluation burst.
- Acceptance gates: eval quality signoff + SOC2 evidence + networking test.

If you’re comfortable, I can propose a MAP with two commitment scenarios: (A) 3-month Dedicated starter pool (fastlane) and (B) Private VPC pilot with a 4-week staging window.

Targeting a draft back to you by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference.com | +1 415-555-0147

Attachment: initial_map_fastlane.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@helixhealth.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procure@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation fastlane: MAP and GPU pool sizing for HelixHealth

Ben —

Appreciate the summary and the clear asks. Confirmations below:
- Go-live window: target week of 2028-06-17 (business critical calendar event week of 6/24 would be risky).
- Deployment: We prefer Dedicated to start (Redwood-managed) for faster turn-up and because our infra team wants to avoid early VPC complexity. Long term we’ll evaluate Private.
- Workload: peak concurrent production ~18–22 inference streams; avg sequence ~400 tokens; spike tests may hit ~40 concurrent for short bursts.
- Procurement windows: we have an internal budget approval deadline 2028-05-10 and a security review kickoff 2028-04-18.

Obstacles: procurement needs a lead-time estimate in writing and a clear acceptance criteria matrix for go/no-go. Also SOC2 evidence and a network diagram will be required for the security review.

Send over the MAP with the two scenarios. If we can show a staged activation plan aligned to the 5/10 budget approval, we’ll try to push the commit earlier.

—Dana
Dana Liu
Head of AI Ops, HelixHealth
dana.liu@helixhealth.com

Attachment: (none)

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T12:38:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Activation fastlane: MAP and GPU pool sizing for HelixHealth

Folks — forwarding Dana’s confirmation and procurement windows. Key items we need to lock in the MAP and the close timeline:

1) Lead-time justification (procurement wants this written): can we attach our H100 lead-time estimate and an alternative Ampere/RTX path? I’ve asked for a PDF estimate — attaching H100_leadtime_estimate.pdf.

2) Sizing recs: Dana gave peak/avg numbers. For a Dedicated starter pool I’m thinking:
   - Option Alpha (conservative): 6x H100 equivalent (handles 40 concurrent spike headroom + 30% buffer)
   - Option Beta (cost-conscious): 3x H100 equivalent + autoscale policies to burst to a shared pool during spikes

3) Acceptance gates to include in MAP: eval pass (top-3 prompt templates), perf SLOs (p95 latency < 350ms for 400-token avg), SOC2 checklist items, and network cutover test.

4) Timeline: to hit Dana’s go-live week (2028-06-17) with the 12–14 week lead time, we need a signed commitment by 2028-04-23 to place orders and begin provisioning. That aligns with their 5/10 budget approval window only if we can show an SOW addendum or LOI before 5/10.

I drafted MAP_Workbook_v2.xlsx with the two scenarios and lane-level milestones (attached). Please review the sizing assumptions and the acceptance criteria language — Priyom, can you add the exact SLO phrasing and the rollback plan? Marissa, can you propose commercial terms for Alpha vs Beta (monthly vs reserved)?

Thanks — I’ll stitch the docset and send to Dana and Procurement Ops once we have internal alignment.

—Ben

Attachments: H100_leadtime_estimate.pdf (pdf), MAP_Workbook_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Activation fastlane: MAP and GPU pool sizing for HelixHealth

Ben / Priyom —

Reviewed and updated the workbook. Highlights of changes I made:
- Commercial lanes: defined Alpha as a 6x H100 reserved tranche with a 9-month minimum and a 12% commit discount; Beta as a 3x H100 starter with 3-month term + burst-to-shared pricing.
- Acceptance: tightened perf SLO language to include token-accuracy regression threshold (no more than 2% drop vs baseline prompts) and a rolling canary policy during cutover.
- Procurement artifact: added a short one-page 'Lead Time and Activation Assumptions' (see activation_checklist.txt) that procurement can attach to their approval packet.

Net-net: with Dana’s 5/10 budget milestone we still need a LOI by 4/23 to guarantee the H100 tranche arrival before 6/17. If LOI misses 4/23 we move to the Beta plan (smaller pool + burst) and extend go-live to late June.

Priyom — please confirm the rollback cadence (how we scale down the tranche if utilization stays low) and add the exact canary traffic routing steps. I’ll inline the updated commercial bullets into the MAP and send to Dana + Proc by EOD.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com

Attachment: activation_checklist.txt (txt); MAP_Workbook_v2.xlsx (updated)
